prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: individual Bible Journey illustration of Paul’s athletic metaphor in Philippians 3:12–14, landscape 1536×1024, full frame, no interface or text.
Input images: Image 1 and Image 2 are approved style references only. Match their warm cinematic realism, natural proportions, tactile materials, nuanced light, and readable composition. Do not reproduce their scenes, characters, or compositions.
Scene/backdrop: One symbolic runner presses toward a mark, illustrating Paul’s words. This is a literary comparison, not a documented race or named historical event.
Subject/action: Show one fully clothed adult athlete in simple period-evocative running clothes, moving forward in a determined but natural stride. A plain low finish marker stands just ahead within the left half; the runner leans and reaches forward toward it. Keep the person distinct and dignified, without modern sports gear or a literal trophy.
Composition/framing: Use a wider view from several paces away; the full runner should occupy about 60% of the canvas height. Place the top of the runner’s head below the 18% line and the feet above the 84% line; leave generous open sky above and ground below, and do not crop any part. Keep runner and marker fully within the left 60%. Reserve the right 30% as quiet open ground and soft sky for a reading panel. One continuous symbolic composition.
Style/materials: Warm realistic historical illustration; natural face and hands, simple woven garment and leather footwear, textured earth, restrained earth pigments, soft directional light.
Constraints: The runner and marker illustrate Paul’s metaphor, not a historical sporting event. No crowd, stadium, route map, text, inscriptions, crown, modern gear, banners, pins, logos, border, or watermark.
notes: Final raster reviewed against the named subjects; account-specific references remain in the scene registry. Historical appearances are reconstructed and literary scenes are labeled.
